Subject: Finova performance SLO & multi-region routing — post-call recap

Thanks Lina and Rajiv — great conversation today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key requirements you mentioned:
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for up to 1k token generations (for consumer-facing flows). p99 target to be discussed for high-priority requests.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state ~120 req/s across API, peak bursts to ~300 req/s; peak concurrent streams ~60.
- Streaming: important for frontend UX — server-sent events (chunked token streaming) required.
- Multi-region routing / data residency: US primary, EU traffic must remain in EU data centers (data residency/regulatory constraint), APAC routing for low-latency experience in Singapore/Japan.
- Fallbacks: prefer automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model in case of capacity issues; want graceful degradation not outright failures.

Attachments: SLO-matrix-v1.xlsx (SLO table we discussed), redwood-dataplane-arch.pdf (high-level routing options).

Deliverables / next steps:
1) We’ll send a proposed SLO matrix (attached) and three routing options: hosted multi-region, dedicated region pinning, and hybrid with regional caching.
2) Engineering sizing question: can you confirm concurrent streaming sessions during peak minutes vs average? You mentioned 50–70 concurrent for product A — if you can send exact numbers per flow that’s ideal.
3) Security/residency: please loop in your security/compliance contact and we’ll share the data flow diagram + SOC2 artifacts.
4) Next meeting: propose Wed 11/11 10:00 PT to review SLO matrix and mutual action plan. Let us know if that works.

Thanks,

Rajiv — some quick answers and clarifying asks from our side: 
- Latency measurement: we usually report server-side p95/p99 measured at the inference gateway (excluding last-mile client RTT). We can provide both server-side and synthetic end-to-end benchmarks.
- Streaming resume: supported for our dedicated/private deployments via session tokens + KV-backed resume. For hosted API we support reconnects and token-level resume for short disconnects (we’ll outline exact window limits).
- Data residency: we can pin inference and log storage to EU-only infrastructure for your EU traffic — this is available on Dedicated and Private planes; for Hosted we offer EU regional tenancy with KMS-backed keys and retention controls.

Sizing notes needed from you: average tokens per request (prompt + completion), number of multi-turn chat sessions kept warm (KV cache impact), and expected percent of traffic requiring streaming vs non-streaming. With that we’ll propose either:
A) Hosted multi-region config with regional endpoints + EU-only log storage
B) Dedicated regional pools (EU pinned) with cross-region routing for failover
C) Hybrid: EU pinned Dedicated for regulated flows + hosted elsewhere for cost efficiency

I’ve attached a short draft mutual action plan we can iterate on.
